method.candidate: newly occupied non-ground cell spatially associated with a person at the display snapshot; not a semantic per-voxel label
method.departure: all people farther than 0.9m in XY and no robot body at this location
method.visibility: current sensor within 12m effective range and vertical FOV; evaluation ray along voxel center must have first physical return beyond the voxel; no return or intervening hit is not certified exposure
method.clearance: occupied disappears from complete display set in same epoch; display does not distinguish free from unknown
method.timing: simulation seconds, sampled about every wall second; temporal bounds retained; map fusion/decimation can delay observations; line-of-sight does not prove an actual discrete scan ray intersected the cell

summary.timing_warning: prior line-of-sight is not proof of continuous scan exposure; delayed fusion and discretization remain possible
limitations: Only six spatially associated newly occupied voxels were tracked, not every human footprint or all old map residue.
All six were already absent at the first sample where people were >0.9m away; precise disappearance time and causal source (LiDAR versus depth) were not isolated.
No candidate remained occupied long enough after departure to obtain the scheduled visibility raycast; no occlusion-certified clearing-delay claim is made.
No claim about required clearing outside sensor visibility is made.
Range/FOV reconstruction uses fixed vertical profile mounts and level-body contract; it is evaluation-only.
